key_insight: A plug-and-play concept bottleneck approach can debug medical imaging models by testing and intervening on human-interpretable concepts rather than treating the model as a black box.
clinical_relevance: This could help clinicians and developers identify whether a model is relying on meaningful findings or spurious correlations, making model refinement more transparent and targeted.
method: Align a single-modality encoder to BioMedCLIP to build a Concept Bottleneck Model.
Use concept-level interventions to separate causal concepts from spuriously correlated ones.
Generate counterfactual samples and use guided fine-tuning to refine model behavior.
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated on a Mayo Clinic ultrasound dataset and the CheXpert 5x200 chest X-ray dataset, with results showing reliable model diagnosis and sometimes improved predictive performance after guided fine-tuning.
watch_item: Concept-based debugging depends on the quality and completeness of the chosen concepts, so missing or poorly defined concepts could limit interpretability and intervention utility.
paper_title: Beyond Explanation: Debugging Medical Imaging Models via Concept Intervention
